title: Linguistic fallback + heatmap contrast & keyboard nav sweep for cost rollouts
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket is a combined design sweep to resolve outstanding WCAG color contrast failures and to formalize keyboard navigation and linguistic fallback behavior for the cost heatmap and rollout variant inspector. The goal is to ship a set of UI changes and a validation kit that ensures: (1) color ramps meet 4.5:1 where text is used, (2) focus order is deterministic across expanded/collapsed rows and variant panes, and (3) localized labels fall back gracefully (language order preference + short-form tokens) without truncation or layout shift.

Scope of work (design deliverables):
- Visual token adjustments for heatmap color ramps and legend swatches (desktop and compact views).
- Revised focus styles and tabindex guidance for rows, variant inspector, and the rollout timeline scrubber.
- Content strategy for i18n fallbacks: primary label, secondary short token, and tooltip fallback.
- Prototypes in Figma for high/low density table modes and expanded variant inspector with keyboard-only flows.
- Accessibility validation checklist (manual + automated) and sample screen reader narration notes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Heatmap text and numeric labels meet contrast 4.5:1 on all supported palettes; alternative patterns proposed where contrast cannot be achieved without losing semantic meaning.
- Keyboard-only users can: open/close variant inspector, move between heatmap rows, toggle rollout variants, and activate variant-level actions without mouse. Documented keystrokes exist and are implemented with appropriate ARIA roles.
- Localized labels: when a translation is missing or truncated, a deterministic fallback shows: (1) short token from the model tag, (2) English microcopy, then (3) tooltip with full source label. No UI overflow or layout jump in 10 major locales (en, fr, de, es, pt-BR, ja, ko, zh-Hans, ru, nl).
- Edge cases documented: extremely long numeric formats, RTL languages, and unit abbreviations.
- Figma prototype links and a Confluence spec are attached and approved by Accessibility and Intl leads.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Decided to keep heatmap hue semantics intact and adjust label contrast instead of switching to monochrome patterns to preserve quick visual scanning for power users.
- For very dense tables, we propose a contextual callout pattern (non-modal) rather than moving to modal dialogs to avoid focus trap complexity in long lists.
- Chose to implement a lightweight aria-live terse update for rollout status changes to avoid verbose screen reader noise on frequent refreshes.

Implementation notes for ENG:
- Provide CSS tokens: --heatmap-label-on-dark, --heatmap-label-on-light, and a density modifier class (density-compact).
- Engineering to add data-attribute hooks for keyboard focus management: data-kb-target and data-kb-group.
- Provide aria-roledescription for variant rows and ensure role=\"button\" on keyboard-activatable elements.

Links and artifacts:
- Figma prototype: https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/heatmap-intl-keynav-2026
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/567890/Heatmap+Intl+and+Keyboard+Sweep
- GitHub draft PR (styles + focus helpers): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4221
- Accessibility checklist (doc): https://drive.google.com/file/d/REDACTED/view

QA & validation plan:
- Manual pass across VoiceOver (macOS), NVDA (Windows), TalkBack (Android) for the keyboard flows.
- Automated contrast audit with Axe & pa11y integrated into the PR pipeline.
- Localization smoke tests with sample translations for 10 locales.

Next steps after design acceptance:
- Finalize CSS token names and handoff to ENG with a 2-week implementation window (see ENG estimate).
- Schedule a follow-up verification session with Accessibility and Intl engineers during the first rollout.
